newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's Ecobank raises capital base four-fold.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's Ecobank raises capital base four-fold.

text.p: Ecobank Nigeria Plc said it had raised its capital base to 534 million naira from 133.5 million, surpassing new government requirements that banks operating in Nigeria should have a minimum capitalisation of 500 million naira from 50 million naira previously.

The bank's chairman Adekunle Ojora told the annual general meeting in Lagos on Tuesday that shareholders would benefit from the increase through a bonus issue of three new shares for every existing share.
He said gross earnings of the bank increased to 1.5 billion naira in the year ended September 1996 from 888 million naira, an increase of 69 percent.
"Profits after tax also increased by 83 percent from 254 million naira in 1995 to 466 million naira in 1996," he said.

Ecobank Nigeria Plc is a subsidiary of the Ecobank Transnational Incorporated (ETI), a private sector financial institution established by authority of the heads of state of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).
ETI as a holding company of Ecobank has other subsidiaries in Ghana, Ivory Coast, Benin, Burkina Faso and Togo.
ETI holds 40 percent of the Ecobank in Nigeria while the balance is held by Nigerian citizens and other investors.
